noise: marginal cc bootstrap SE about 4.9 pp (research/24); cache-path flips 1-4 items. The 2.0 pp gate threshold is a paired difference on the same 231 items: its SE is sqrt(discordant)/n, about 2.7-3.1 pp for a real arm (38-52 discordant), so 2.0 pp is about 0.7 paired SE
default_gate_for_v4_arms: paired on the same 231 items, tree and path. Primary test: exact McNemar on per-item correctness (model/scripts/paired_mcnemar.py). promote if arm wins > losses with two-sided p < 0.05, cc >= control + 2.0 pp, and hard >= control - 1.0 pp; kill if cc <= control or losses > wins with p < 0.05; otherwise inconclusive: add seeds 43/44, pool their discordant pairs, and promote only if the pooled exact McNemar has p < 0.05 with wins > losses. The 2.0 pp is an effect-size floor, not the significance test: with 38-52 discordant items it is about 0.7 paired SE, so it never promotes alone

The canonical run excludes 1,479 train rows with answerable=False (the none_of_these abstention rows) keyed on the flag, not on _label_index<0. Verified on the corpus: 2,000 choice rows have no label among the criteria keys, all 2,000 are answerable=False, and no answerable row has a negative index. An answerable row with a negative index now raises with its id. Interim measure: drop and mask are gradient-equivalent only in this per-item loop; the answerable head (#254) should replace the filter. Separately, 1,905 canonical score rows carry a fractional label (674 at 2.5, 672 at 1.5, 313 at 3.5, 157 at 0.5, 89 at other decimals); _label_index rounds them, 1,521 in the train split. Routed to the corpus owner; the trainer does not change the rounding.

The 1,905 fractional score labels are two populations. Authored midpoints: 0.5 (157), 1.5 (672), 2.5 (674), 3.5 (313), 1,816 total. Arbitrary fractions: 2.2 (18), 2.8 (14), 3.2 (13), 3.8 (10), 1.7 (5), 1.8 (5), 1.3 (4), 1.2 (4), and 25 others, 89 total; these suggest a free-form numeric answer or a generator that did not respect the scale, which is a different phenomenon from approved midpoints. The trainer rounds with int(round(float(label))) (banker rounding at x.5) and does not mask or relabel; the fix belongs in the consumer. Gate-facing exposure: frozen held-out has 786 score rows, 0 fractional; JevBench has 18 score rows, 0 fractional, so no standard C gate metric uses a rounded label. The train split has 1,521 fractional rows and the internal val split 384; those affect only early stopping, which is not the gate. The gate JSON records the method and the two denominators.

The frozen held-out has 6,424 ids but evaluates 6,254 under the current label-index metric: 170 choice rows are answerable=False abstention rows inside the held-out clusters and have no label index. By type the evaluated set is noul 2,995 / choice 2,473 / score 786. Every gate row must report n=6,254 of 6,424 and name the 170 as abstention rows; the answerable head (#254) is what makes them scorable. Base and adapter predictions skip the same rows, so the paired test uses the same 6,254 on both sides.
